f.title: Fully consider the purpose and necessity of a post-marketing study before conducting it
f.statement: When a post-marketing study is conducted, it is important to clarify a research question based on pre-marketing clinical trial information and the characteristics of the target disease and drug, and to conduct the study properly; the purpose and necessity of a post-marketing study should be fully considered so that it is not conducted aimlessly.

f.applicability: English translation (PMDA reference translation; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSB/PED and PSB/PSD Notification No. 0718-1 (18 Jul 2024), partially revising PSEHB/PED and PSEHB/PSD Notification No. 0314-4 (14 Mar 2019). Rows are taken from the revised consolidated text attached for reference, unless the location says comparison table.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: When a post-marketing study is conducted, it is important to clarify a research question based on the information obtained from pre-marketing clinical trials, the characteristics of target diseases and the drugs of interest, etc. and to conduct the study properly afterwards. At the same time, it should be noted that the purpose and the necessity of a post-marketing study should be fully considered to prevent the study from being conducted aimlessly.

f.statement: The research question is a specific and clear aim of a study, including population, intervention (exposure), comparator, outcome (efficacy/safety specifications of interest) and timing; study design, the effect measure to be evaluated and the data source should be carefully considered based on it.

f.title: Implement a post-marketing study when a specific efficacy concern arises
f.statement: Efficacy data are generally collected in pre-marketing trials and evaluated to a certain level at approval; if no specific efficacy concern is raised, efficacy could be evaluated by other means (e.g. literature analysis). Where a specific concern about efficacy arises during the approval review or in the post-marketing phase, a post-marketing study should be implemented so that the concern can be scientifically verified.

f.title: Agree Steps 1-3 of the pharmacovigilance plan with PMDA before approval
f.statement: Pharmacovigilance plan development can be divided into four steps: (1) concretising concerns to be clarified post-marketing for each safety specification, (2) determining a scientifically appropriate approach for each concern, (3) confirming the legal and regulatory framework under which each approach is compiled, and (4) developing the study protocol. In principle, the applicant should reach agreement with PMDA on Steps 1-3 before approval.
f.clause: Attachment (revised text): introduction (four steps)
f.applicability: English translation (PMDA reference translation; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSB/PED and PSB/PSD Notification No. 0718-1 (18 Jul 2024), partially revising PSEHB/PED and PSEHB/PSD Notification No. 0314-4 (14 Mar 2019). Rows are taken from the revised consolidated text attached for reference, unless the location says comparison table.

In principle, an applicant should reach an agreement with the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (hereinafter referred to as “PMDA”) about Step 1-3 before the approval.

f.title: Emphasise risk minimisation for important identified risks; study only for a clarified purpose
f.statement: For important identified risks, where the causal relationship is well established, emphasis should basically be placed on risk minimisation activities; where more detailed information (common time of onset, most appropriate treatment, risk factors, etc.) is considered necessary, it may be better to clarify the purpose and consider conducting a study.
f.clause: Attachment (revised text): Step 1) Concretization of concerns
f.applicability: English translation (PMDA reference translation; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSB/PED and PSB/PSD Notification No. 0718-1 (18 Jul 2024), partially revising PSEHB/PED and PSEHB/PSD Notification No. 0314-4 (14 Mar 2019). rows.quote: Regarding “important identified risks,” because a causal relationship between the drug and the adverse event has been well established, emphasis should be basically placed on risk minimization activities. However, when more detailed information regarding the common time of onset, the most appropriate treatment, the identification of risk factors, etc., is considered to be necessary, it may be better to clarify the purpose and consider conducting a study.

f.statement: The second step is to determine the most scientifically appropriate approach for each concern from Step 1, by referring to the annex of the ICH E2E Guideline; depending on the concern, passive surveillance alone (spontaneous reports, literature analysis) could be chosen, and post-marketing studies are not necessary for all concerns.

f.title: Small sample size or missing populations alone do not always justify a survey or study
f.statement: If a small sample size (overall or Japanese subpopulation) or lack of information in some patient populations in a clinical trial is the only concern, it will not always justify a survey or study even if specified as important missing information; a drug use-results survey has limited significance for investigating the frequency of an important identified risk.

f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: If a small sample size (overall study population or Japanese subpopulation) or a lack of information in some patient populations in a clinical trial is the only concern, it will not always serve as a rationale for conducting a survey or study even if such a concern is specified as “important missing information.” A drug use-results survey has limited significance for the purpose of investigating the frequency of an important identified risk.

f.title: Step 3: identify the regulatory framework (GVP, GPSP) for each approach
f.statement: Identify the regulatory framework under which the approach from Step 2 must be compiled: collection of spontaneous reports and literature is routine pharmacovigilance under the GVP Ordinance (MHLW Ordinance No. 135, 2004); a post-marketing study conducted as additional pharmacovigilance is subject to the GPSP Ordinance (MHLW Ordinance No. 171, 2004) in addition to GVP.
f.clause: Attachment (revised text): Step 3) Confirmation of legal and regulatory framework

Rows are taken from the revised consolidated text attached for reference, unless the location says comparison table.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Reporting policy

rows.quote: Identify a regulatory framework where the approach determined in Step 2 must be compiled. Collection of spontaneous reports and literature etc. is conducted as “Routine Pharmacovigilance” in accordance with the Ministerial Ordinance on Good Vigilance Practice for Drugs, Quasi-drugs, Cosmetics, and Medical Devices (MHLW Ordinance No. 135, 2004; hereinafter referred to as “GVP”). On the other hand, a post-marketing study conducted as “Additional Pharmacovigilance” is subject to the Ministerial Ordinance on Good Post-marketing Study Practice for Drugs (MHLW Ordinance No. 171, 2004; hereinafter referred to as “GPSP”) in addition to the GVP.
rows.location: Attachment (revised text): Step 3) Confirmation of legal and regulatory framework

f.title: Classify GPSP studies as drug use-results survey, database study or post-marketing clinical trial
f.statement: Additional pharmacovigilance under GPSP is generally categorised by data collection: information from routine practice collected directly at medical institutions is a drug use-results survey; information obtained from a medical information database is a post-marketing database study; information not collectable in routine practice (i.e. with interventions such as a specific examination) is a post-marketing clinical trial.
f.clause: Attachment (revised text): Step 3) Confirmation of legal and regulatory framework
f.applicability: English translation (PMDA reference translation; the Japanese original prevails) of MHLW PSB/PED and PSB/PSD Notification No. 0718-1 (18 Jul 2024), partially revising PSEHB/PED and PSEHB/PSD Notification No. 0314-4 (14 Mar 2019). f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: When information in routine clinical practice is collected directly in medical institutions, the study is categorized as a “drug use-results survey.” ⚫ When information is obtained from the medical information database, the study is categorized as a “post-marketing database study.” ⚫ When information that cannot be collected in routine clinical practice, such as an implementation of a specific examination, is obtained (i.e., when interventions are conducted), the study is categorized as a “post-marketing clinical trial.”

f.title: Refer to PMDA pharmacoepidemiology guideline and database protocol instructions for database studies
f.statement: When developing protocols for post-marketing database studies, refer to the PMDA "Guidelines for the Conduct of Pharmacoepidemiological Studies in Drug Safety Assessment with Medical Information Databases" (31 Mar 2014) and "Instructions for Post-marketing Database Study Protocols" (23 Jan 2018) on the PMDA website, in addition to the notifications related to pharmacovigilance.
